hints: Use the logarithm laws on the right: $2\ln x=\ln(x^2)$ and subtracting $\ln2$ forms a quotient.
Since the logarithms are equal, equate their positive arguments and solve the resulting equation in $x^2$.
Apply the original domain condition $x>0$ before stating the exact solution.
walkthrough:
Apply the power and quotient laws of logarithms to the right-hand side:
$$2\ln x - \ln 2 = \ln(x^2) - \ln 2 = \ln\left(\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)$$

Equate the arguments of the natural logarithms on both sides:
$$\ln(2x^2 - 3) = \ln\left(\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)$$
$$2x^2 - 3 = \dfrac{x^2}{2}$$

Multiply both sides by 2 to clear the fraction:
$$4x^2 - 6 = x^2$$
$$3x^2 = 6$$
$$x^2 = 2$$
Check the original domain of definition: $\ln x$ requires $x > 0$, so the negative solution $x = -\sqrt{2}$ must be rejected.

Conclude with the single exact positive solution:
$$x = \sqrt{2}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equa: Applies a logarithm law on a term, e.g. $2\ln x=\ln x^2$. Remove logarithms and derives an equation, e.g. $2x^2-3=x^2/2$. The final result is $x=\sqrt2$.
